newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Burma, Laos formally join ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Burma, Laos formally join ASEAN.

text.p: Burma and Laos were formally admitted as the newest members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Wednesday, but Cambodia was left on the sidelines due to its political troubles.
At a ceremony during its 30th anniversary meetings, Burma and Laos foreign ministers signed documents of admission which were then turned over to the ASEAN secretariat.

Last-ditch efforts by Cambodia to gain entry into the regional grouping, which also includes Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, had prompted speculation it might also be admitted on Wednesday.

But ASEAN stuck to a decision it made on July 10, when it said Cambodia's membership would be postponed indefinitely after the country's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen violently ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Cambodia's inclusion in ASEAN would fulfill the group's dream of having all 10 Southeast Asian countries in its fold.

Burma's admission has been harshly criticised by the United States and other Western nations, who want Rangoon isolated for its human rights record and crackdown on the pro-democracy movement. ASEAN has maintained that its policy of "constructive engagement" was the best way of reforming Burma's military rulers.
